newsitem.title: USA: Firm questions Grigsby's disclosure on swap deal.
newsitem.headline: Firm questions Grigsby's disclosure on swap deal.

text.p: A syndicate member on a recent $183 million Florida swap deal has questioned whether or not Grigsby Brandford & Co Inc, senior manager on the deal, properly disclosed a key feature of the offering to investors, sources close to the situation said.
Grigsby Brandford, a San Francisco-based firm, was senior manager on the $183 million revenue bond refunding for Dade County. Grigsby Brandford declined to comment.
Smith Barney Inc was co-senior manager and AIBC Investment Services Corp and Howard Gary & Co were co-managers in the syndicate.

Howard Gary & Co wrote Grigsby Brandford four days before the Dade County deal closed on September 10 asking why it did not disclose in the official statement that the swaps provider, GBR Financial Products, is part owned by Calvin Grigsby and Napolean Brandford, owners and founders of Grigsby Brandford, the sources said, who asked not to be identified.
An official at Howard Gary & Co, citing company policy, declined to comment.
Grigsby Brandford did not respond to Howard Gary's request, according to the sourcs.

The letter to Grigsby Brandford says: "This letter is written to inform you of the firm's concern with respect to the appropriate and timely disclosure under federal, Florida and other applicable local disclosure laws," the sources said.
The letter asks: "Why was the relationship by and between Grigsby Brandford & Co Inc and GBR Financial Products not disclosed in the official statement?"
The letter requests a "legal opinion from co-underwriter counsel" on whether or not Grigsby Brandford's decision not to disclose the relationship in the official statement is "appropriate."
The letter also asks the firm how much it made on the swap and on whose books is the swap transaction being carried.
The $183 million Dade County deal is one of a number of bond issues federal investigatorts are reviewing.

The Miami Herald reported on Thursday that FBI videotapes show Calvine Grigsby allegedly offering a Dade County, Fla., official a $300,000 kickback in exchange for steering the $183 million bond deal to Grigsby's firm. Also at the meeting was Howard Gary, owner of Miami-based Howard Gary & Co.
Calvin Grigsby resigned from San Francisco-based Grigsby Brandford on September 17.
